s1.p1: In this section we will learn about logical values, logical variables, logical expressions and logical operators.
s2.p1: When a person declares that his son is 18 years old, that statement will be true for one year, but before that year and after that year, that statement will be a lie. And that is on the condition that this person has a son.
s2.p2: Suppose a man wrote this statement on his social media page when he was 15 years old.
s2.p3: He did not yet have a son, and the statement was false.
s2.p4: Then he grew up, got married and had a son, but the statement remained false because his son was not yet 18.
s2.p5: Finally, when his son turned 18, the statement became true.
s2.p6: But it lasted for one year.
s2.p7: Then his son turned 19, and this statement became false again.
s2.p8: Thus, this statement is a **variable**. For its meaning can change.
s2.p9: The values this variable can take are **⟦f0⟧** or **⟦f1⟧**
s2.p12: ![ico-25 warn] **There are no other logical values.
s2.p13: ^^We don't have such a sly value as ‘Not everything is so unambiguous’. Everything is unambiguous. It's either black or white. Our world is simple.^^
s2.p14: So, our variable can take one of two possible logical values (**⟦f0⟧** or **⟦f1⟧**).
s3.p1: The statement '_The apple is red and round_' can be decomposed into two parts: '_Apple is red_' + '_Apple is round_'.
s3.p3: Let the boolean variable **⟦f3⟧** take the value **⟦f0⟧** when the property **⟦f27⟧** has the value ‘red’ and the boolean variable **⟦f5⟧** take the value **⟦f0⟧** when the property **⟦f6⟧** has the value ‘round’.
s3.p5: Then the variable **⟦f7⟧** is already a **logical expression**, because it requires its value to be calculated based on the values of the variables **⟦f3⟧** and **⟦f5⟧**.
s3.p6: And this logical expression will have the value **⟦f0⟧** only when both variables **⟦f3⟧** and **⟦f5⟧** have the value **⟦f0⟧**.
s3.p7: A **Logical Expression** is an expression whose evaluation will result in a logical value.
s3.p8: The simplest case of a logical expression is a logical value.
s3.p9: Let's see how we can construct more complex logical expressions.
s4.p1: The simplest way to construct logical expressions is to use **comparison operators**.
s4.p2: These are binary operators, meaning they have two operands.
s4.p3: The operands can be variables or expressions.
s4.p4: ![ico-25 warn] Comparison operators compare not only the **values** but also the **data types** of the operands.
s4.p5: Comparison operators always return a **logical value**.
s4.p7: | **⟦f8⟧**  | non-strict equality ^^(only operand values are compared, under the bonnet, data types are converted)^^ |
s4.p8: | **⟦f9⟧** | strict equality ^^(operand data types are compared, and if the operand data type is the same, the operand values are compared)^^ |
s4.p9: | **⟦f10⟧**  | non-strict inequality ^^(values are not equal, data type is ignored)^^ |
s4.p10: | **⟦f11⟧** | strict inequality ^^(will return ⟦f0⟧ if the data types or values are not equal)^^ |
s4.p16: Each character has a numeric code, and the character codes are compared.
